blocks.c: I got in the car at 03:11 on the twenty-first of March with both log books, a torch, and a printed copy of every photograph I had taken since the beginning, because Wen had said the word document four times and I had started to think about what that meant.
I pressed the unnumbered button four times.
Minus one: the empty lobby. Minus two: the dark corridor. Minus three: the landing.
The mop bucket was there, upturned. Her head torch was on the floor beside it, still on, pointing at the wall, batteries almost gone.
On the fire door, in wet ink, in block capitals, at the height of a person's shoulder:
IT MOVED ME. THIS IS ALLOWED — I CHECKED. IT IS NOT ALLOWED TO STOP YOU FOLLOWING.
BRING THE BOOKS. DO NOT PRESS THE BUTTON MORE THAN ONCE PER FLOOR AND WRITE THE FLOOR DOWN EACH TIME, IN INK, BEFORE YOU PRESS.
IF THE NUMBERS EVER GO OUT OF ORDER, GET OUT AT THE NEXT DOOR AND WALK.
I picked up her head torch and turned it off, because the batteries were nearly gone and because I have never in my life been able to leave a light on in an empty room.
Then I got back in the freight car and wrote MINUS FOUR in the log, in ink, and pressed the button once.
I looked at the sign on the wall opposite, which was the standard Merridew floor sign, aluminium, riveted, exactly like the thirty-one upstairs.
